47.0.s.en: (1) The striking of Palestine by Egypt and Babylon

47.0.0.en: The book sets the time of this prophecy as before Pharaoh Necho’s striking of Gaza. This time is not known exactly, but it is in the late seventh century and the beginning of the sixth century BC. This king of Egypt may have struck it on his way to Carchemish on the river Euphrates, or on his return from it after his defeat at the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, or on his return from the attempt to rescue Jerusalem when the king of Babylon struck it in 587 BC. This Palestine entered into wars with the people of God in the days of Samson, in the days of Samuel and in the days of David the prophet, so it bore enmity toward the children of Israel. God, who was patient with it for many years, now allows its chastening and destruction, so that its people may be humbled, turn away from their violence and believe in God. This indeed happened, for many of them believed in Christ.

47.0.1.en: The striking of Gaza is the striking of a famous Philistine city, and what is meant by it is the striking of Gaza itself, or the beginning of the striking of all the cities of Palestine.

47.1.0.en: The prophecy is about Babylon’s attack on Palestine. He likens Babylon to a sweeping flood of water coming from the north, because they have the great river Euphrates; it comes upon the land of Palestine and destroys it with all that is in it and kills those who dwell in it, and the Philistines cry out with bitter weeping at the horror of the destruction.

47.2.0.en: Rushing and rumbling (noise of the stamping and rattling): the sound of the iron of the chariots rubbing against each other, and the sound of the chariot wheels scraping the ground. Feebleness of hands (slack hands): great weakness and fear. Babylon attacks with its horsemen and war chariots and kills and destroys the cities of Palestine, and the Philistines flee in great panic, so that in their weakness they leave their children behind them.

47.2.1.en: Do not be harsh in your dealings with those around you, relying on your strength, for it is liable to pass away. Know that God is just and able to chasten you severely, but He is longsuffering toward you, that perhaps you may repent and have mercy on those around you and forgive them their faults.

47.2.3.en: 4- Because of the day that cometh to spoil all the Philistines, and to cut off from Tyrus and Zidon every helper that remaineth: for the LORD will spoil the Philistines, the remnant of the country of Caphtor.

47.2.4.en: The day that cometh: the day of Babylon’s attack on Palestine and its allies. Tyre: a city in Lebanon lying on the Mediterranean Sea, an important commercial port. The meaning of the word Tyre is “rock”, because it is built on rocks.

47.2.5.en: Sidon: a city in Lebanon lying on the Mediterranean Sea, south of Tyre. The meaning of the word is “a place of fishing”, because it is famous for fishing.

47.2.7.en: In Babylon’s attack on the Philistines to lay waste their land, they also attacked their allies Tyre and Sidon, and also the island of Crete, from which the Philistines came to the land named after them. With the destruction of the allies, the Philistines find no help against the Babylonian attack.

47.2.8.en: Let your reliance be on God and not on the powers of the world, for they are passing and weak however strong they appear. Take refuge in God by prayer in all your needs.

47.2.9.en: [3] The pagan gods do not benefit Palestine (vv. 5-7:)

47.2.10.en: 5- Baldness is come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is cut off with the remnant of their valley: how long wilt thou cut thyself? 6- O thou sword of the LORD, how long will it be ere thou be quiet? put up thyself into thy scabbard, rest, and be still. 7- How can it be quiet, seeing the LORD hath given it a charge against Ashkelon, and against the sea shore? there hath he appointed it.

47.3.0.en: Cut thyself: you wound your body. Their valley: the valleys surrounding the cities. He likens Gaza to a girl on whose head baldness has come, so that she lost her hair; what is meant is that she lost her standing and became weak like a girl in her bodily weakness, and the strong cities of Palestine such as Ashkelon were destroyed. Palestine tried to seek help from its pagan gods and to cut its body to please them, but in vain, for its gods did not help it against the Babylonian attack.

47.4.0.en: Scabbard: the sheath in which the sword is placed. He calls Babylon the sword of the LORD, which chastens the Philistines, and the prophet sees the cruelty of the destruction or killing that Babylon carries out on Palestine, so the prophet is moved and calls on the LORD to stop this destruction or killing.

47.5.0.en: God answers in the prophecy that the sword will continue to kill, because God has commanded it so, as a chastening of the Philistines for their violence.

47.5.1.en: Since the world is changeable and you can lose your strength at any time, be detached from material things and use them in measure, for asceticism is beautiful against the violence of changes. Be satisfied with the love of God, and you will live happily and prepare your soul for eternity.

48.0.0.en: God declares the ruin of Moab, which lies east of the river Jordan, north of the children of Ammon. He mentions its famous cities as a symbol of all Moab. The city of Nebo lies beside Mount Abarim, east of the Jordan opposite Jericho, and beside it are the cities of Kiriathaim and Misgab.

48.1.0.en: Babylon’s attack on Moab destroys their capital Heshbon, and the sword of Babylon kills the people of Moab in the Moabite city of Madmen.

48.2.0.en: As a result of the destruction of the Moabite city of Horonaim and the killing of many, the rest of the Moabites cry out at what has happened to them.

48.3.0.en: As a result of the ruin of Moab, its little ones cry out in fear and terror at what is happening to them.

48.4.0.en: Here he also mentions two Moabite cities, the ascent of Luhith and Horonaim, which lies in a valley beside it. From these cities bitter weeping is heard, for the sorrow of their peoples over the ruin of their land. Because of the corruption of Moab and the spread of evil lusts in it, ruin came upon it at the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, and that was in 582 BC. The Moabites are the descendants of Lot, that is, relatives of the children of Israel, and had a relationship with the people of God in the days of the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Then after the children of Israel settled in the Promised Land, there were disputes and wars between them until David subdued the Moabites. Then Moab was destroyed by Assyria, and when it afterward tried to regain its strength, it was destroyed by the Moabites of whom Jeremiah speaks here; then it submitted afterward to Persian rule and after that to the Arabs.

48.4.1.en: Do not go on and on in your lusts, lest divine justice come upon you and your end be destruction, but sanctify your senses and your thoughts to be for God, and you will live in reassurance.

48.4.3.en: 6- Flee, save your lives, and be like the heath in the wilderness. 7- For because thou hast trusted in thy works and in thy treasures, thou shalt also be taken: and Chemosh shall go forth into captivity with his priests and his princes together. 8- And the spoiler shall come upon every city, and no city shall escape: the valley also shall perish, and the plain shall be destroyed, as the LORD hath spoken. 9- Give wings unto Moab, that it may flee and get away: for the cities thereof shall be desolate, without any to dwell therein. 10- Cursed be he that doeth the work of the LORD deceitfully, and cursed be he that keepeth back his sword from blood.

48.5.0.en: Heath: a shrub that grows in the desert, with small leaves, which goats eat; it is a symbol of the man who trusts in men, for he loses his strength as the heath loses its leaves when animals eat them. Jeremiah calls the Moabites to flee from the Babylonian attack, and when they reach the desert the Babylonians neglect them, but they are in distress, isolation and weakness like the heath plant.

48.6.0.en: Chemosh: the god of the Moabites, to whom human sacrifices of children were offered. Solomon introduced his worship into Jerusalem, and King Josiah afterward removed it.

48.6.1.en: He rebukes the cities of Moab, which trusted in their strength and their circumstances, for their shame will appear when the Babylonians destroy them and drive out their inhabitants, who go out carrying the images of their god Chemosh in weakness and shame, and thus the priests of Chemosh and the princes of Moab are humbled when Babylon takes them captive.

48.7.0.en: The valley: a vale. Babylon destroys all the cities of Moab, whether those on the heights or in the valleys, because God is the One who commanded this as a chastening of Moab.

48.8.0.en: Jeremiah expresses the Moabites’ fear of Babylon, for they need speed in running, as a bird flies, because the Babylonian attack will be violent and kill everyone it meets.

48.9.0.en: God calls the army of Babylon to kill the Moabites and do the work of the LORD, that is, the destruction of Moab, with all zeal and energy, so that the Babylonians do not slacken in killing the Moabites by the sword. The destruction of Moab is considered the work of the LORD, because they provoked Him with their evil lusts, so He chastens them by the hand of Babylon.

48.9.1.en: All your works, especially if they are service to those around you and care for the salvation of their souls, are the work of the LORD. May you do it with care, because it is the work of the LORD, and offer it to Him before offering it to people. And as Christ cared for the salvation of your soul and accomplished it with all seriousness, so that He died for you, do His work with all energy, however great the sacrifice.

48.9.3.en: 11- Moab hath been at ease from his youth, and he hath settled on his lees, and hath not been emptied from vessel to vessel, neither hath he gone into captivity: therefore his taste remained in him, and his scent is not changed. 12- Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will send unto him wanderers, that shall cause him to wander, and shall empty his vessels, and break their bottles. 13- And Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel their confidence.

48.10.0.en: Lees: the remains of fermented grapes, that is, the sediment found at the bottom of wine bottles.

48.10.1.en: Settled on his lees: this means that Moab is at ease like the wine sediment that does not move at the bottom of the bottles, because no one dares to stir it, that is, to attack Moab.

48.10.2.en: Not emptied from vessel to vessel: the Moabites were not moved from place to place, that is, from their land to another land in captivity.

48.10.3.en: He explains the state of the Moabites, who were living in reassurance inside their land, and likens them to the sediment at the bottom of the wine vessel. No one took them captive except a small number in the days of the Assyrian attack, until the Babylonian attack came and took most of the Moabites captive. That is, Moab lived in peace and ease like wine whose scent is in it and whose taste has not changed, until Babylon attacked it and turned it into a bad state; the bad vessel from which all its goods were poured out was then broken, that is, its goods were taken away and it was shattered.

48.11.0.en: Wanderers that shall cause him to wander (pourers who pour him out): workers, that is, smiths who shape it, and what is meant is that they turn it into a bad vessel. Jeremiah warns Moab that days will come, the days of the Babylonian attack, when they will drive the Moabites from their land and destroy their cities. He likens the cities of Moab to wine vessels, which Babylon overturns, and the wine is spilled and they stir the sediment at the bottom, then break the vessels, that is, destroy the cities. In sum, Babylon will take away Moab’s peace, drive out its inhabitants and destroy its cities.

48.12.0.en: Moab feels its weakness, and the weakness of its god Chemosh, before Babylon, and is ashamed as the kingdom of Israel was ashamed, that is, the northern kingdom whose capital was Samaria, when it trusted in the images that King Jeroboam set up in Bethel when he separated with the ten tribes from the kingdom of Judah and Jerusalem. The weakness of these images appeared, for they did not protect the people from the Assyrian attack and captivity.

48.12.1.en: Trust in God in all your works, for He is able to protect you, and do not trust in your money and your abilities, lest your weakness and shame appear. Use these capacities for God’s sake and with His help, and they will be beneficial to you. [4] The shame of Moab (vv. 14-25:)

48.12.2.en: 14- How say ye, We are mighty and strong men for the war? 15- Moab is spoiled, and gone up out of her cities, and his chosen young men are gone down to the slaughter, saith the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts. 16- The calamity of Moab is near to come, and his affliction hasteth fast. 17- All ye that are about him, bemoan him; and all ye that know his name, say, How is the strong staff broken, and the beautiful rod! 18- Thou daughter that dost inhabit Dibon, come down from thy glory, and sit in thirst; for the spoiler of Moab shall come upon thee, and he shall destroy thy strong holds. 19- O inhabitant of Aroer, stand by the way, and espy; ask him that fleeth, and her that escapeth, and say, What is done? 20- Moab is confounded; for it is broken down: howl and cry; tell ye it in Arnon, that Moab is spoiled, 21- And judgment is come upon the plain country; upon Holon, and upon Jahazah, and upon Mephaath, 22- And upon Dibon, and upon Nebo, and upon Beth-diblathaim, 23- And upon Kiriathaim, and upon Beth-gamul, and upon Beth-meon, 24- And upon Kerioth, and upon Bozrah, and upon all the cities of the land of Moab, far or near.

48.12.3.en: 25- The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken, saith the LORD.

48.13.0.en: Jeremiah marvels at the boasting of the men of Moab in their strength in war, when they have been crushed before the Babylonian attack. This is what he sees by the spirit of prophecy: its people fled from their cities in the plains and went up to the mountains to hide in them, but the sword of Babylon reached them and brought them down slain to the ground. This is the chastening and command of God concerning Moab. In God is all power, so He is called the LORD of hosts, who shatters every evil power on earth that stands in His face, as Moab did.

48.14.0.en: He also declares that the destruction of Moab is very near, so Jeremiah’s prophecy will be fulfilled quickly by Babylon’s attack on Moab.

48.15.0.en: Bemoan him: speak words of lament in which you show its virtues, and weep over it. God calls the cities and nations around Moab to grieve over it, for despite its former greatness it has now been shattered by Babylon. He likens its strength to the golden staff that the king holds, or the rod of authority; that is, it will lose its glory and greatness among the nations and be in great shame before Babylon.

48.16.0.en: Thirst: dry, thirsty land. Dibon: the Moabite city in which stands the god Chemosh, the god of the Moabites; it lies north of the river Arnon, that is, east of the Dead Sea.

48.16.1.en: He declares to Moab that it will come down from its glory and be in hunger and thirst that lead it to death, and its god Chemosh, whom they have set in the city of Dibon, will not profit it, because the army of Babylon, the destroyer of Moab, has attacked its cities and gone up on its walls and fortresses and demolished them.

48.17.0.en: Aroer: a Moabite city north of the river Arnon, which lies east of the Dead Sea; it is 12 miles from the Dead Sea and south-east of Dibon.

48.17.1.en: He shows how amazed the Moabites were at the speed of the Babylonian attack on them. He calls the inhabitants of the city of Aroer to go out onto the roads leading to the rest of the cities of Moab, so that they see people running in flight and ask then what is the reason for their flight, and learn that it is the violent Babylonian attack.

48.18.0.en: Then he calls the Moabites to tell all the cities around the river Arnon, which lies inside the land of Moab, and let them know of the Babylonian attack, so that they flee far away. Thus weeping and fear cover the people of Moab, and they are scattered in flight everywhere.

48.19.0.en: He shows the sweeping of the Babylonian attack over all Moab, and here mentions the most famous cities of Moab that were ruined, to show Babylon’s reaching all the cities of Moab, far and near, and shattering them.

48.20.1.en: The sum is the shattering of Moab’s power before Babylon, which is symbolized by the horn that is broken and the arm that is shattered; the horn and the arm are the strength with which an animal or a man defends or attacks in war.

48.20.2.en: Consider the situations in which you trusted in your strength and the troubles that befell you, so that you take refuge in God and rely on Him, and neither Satan nor all the powers of the world will prevail against you.

48.20.4.en: 26- Make ye him drunken: for he magnified himself against the LORD: Moab also shall wallow in his vomit, and he also shall be in derision.

48.20.5.en: 27- For was not Israel a derision unto thee? was he found among thieves? for since thou spakest of him, thou skippedst for joy. 28- O ye that dwell in Moab, leave the cities, and dwell in the rock, and be like the dove that maketh her nest in the sides of the hole’s mouth. 29- We have heard the pride of Moab, (he is exceeding proud) his loftiness, and his arrogancy, and his pride, and the haughtiness of his heart. 30- I know his wrath, saith the LORD; but it shall not be so; his lies shall not so effect it. 31- Therefore will I howl for Moab, and I will cry out for all Moab; mine heart shall mourn for the men of Kir-heres. 32- O vine of Sibmah, I will weep for thee with the weeping of Jazer: thy plants are gone over the sea, they reach even to the sea of Jazer: the spoiler is fallen upon thy summer fruits and upon thy vintage.

48.21.0.en: He shows the lowliness of Moab before the Babylonian attack, so that it becomes like a drunkard who staggers and has lost his balance and his greatness. He asks the army of Babylon to make him drink the wine, that is, to make him stagger from fear as the drunkard staggers, and from his great drunkenness he vomits what is inside him, so his humiliation increases as he wallows in the vomit he has thrown up, and all the surrounding peoples mock him. All this is because of his pride and his magnifying himself against God and against His people Israel, for Moab used to mock the people of God when distress came upon them or enemies attacked them.

48.22.0.en: Skippedst (you shook the head): you shake your head in mockery and contempt. God rebukes Moab in its shame and declares to it that the cause of this shame is its mocking of the people of God and despising them as though they were wicked thieves, so it used to speak of them with mockery and move its head in contempt of them in their troubles.

48.23.0.en: Leave: vacate, flee and abandon the cities. He calls the Moabites to flee from their cities to the mountains and hide among the rocks, that perhaps they may escape from the hand of Babylon, and likens them to a weak dove that cannot nest safely among the branches of trees but flees to make itself a nest among the rocks in the mountains.

48.24.0.en: Here he affirms that all the surrounding peoples know Moab’s great pride, and because of it this shame came upon it before Babylon.

48.25.0.en: God declares that the wrath of Moab, which used to terrify those around it, is nothing, and its weakness and shame have appeared before Babylon. And all the words of pride that Moab kept repeating are lies, as proved by the shame it received before Babylon.

48.26.0.en: Kir-heres: a Moabite city lying east of the Dead Sea and its southern part.

48.26.1.en: The fatherhood of Jeremiah appears in his weeping over Moab, for he is like his God, who wants the salvation of all and not only of the people of God. He is deeply moved, so he weeps and howls and then cries out with a loud voice because of the ruin of Moab, and within himself he also groans, pained for its sake. He mentions here one of the cities of Moab as a symbol of all the cities of Moab.

48.27.0.en: Jazer: a Moabite city lying north of Moab, ten miles west of Rabbah of Ammon.

48.27.1.en: Sibmah: a Moabite city beside the city of Heshbon, the capital of the Moabites, in the north of the land of Moab; Sibmah was famous for its vineyards.

48.27.3.en: Summer fruits: the fruits gathered from the harvest.

48.27.4.en: Jeremiah continues his feelings of fatherhood toward Moab and weeps over its land, famous for its wealth, such as Jazer and Sibmah, for all its good things, from the clusters of grapes with their branches and the various fruits, were seized by the Babylonians and carried over the sea, that is, the rivers, so that they might enjoy them, after they had destroyed the land of Moab and left its inhabitants who remained after the killing in great poverty.

48.27.5.en: Your pride separates you from God, so you are deprived of His mercies and Satan attacks you, and thus you find no one to help you. Therefore humble yourself quickly and offer repentance before God, and He will forgive you and save you from the enemy.

48.27.6.en: [6] The humiliation and poverty of Moab (vv. 33-39:)

48.27.7.en: 33- And joy and gladness is taken from the plentiful field, and from the land of Moab; and I have caused wine to fail from the winepresses: none shall tread with shouting; their shouting shall be no shouting. 34- From the cry of Heshbon even unto Elealeh, and even unto Jahaz, have they uttered their voice, from Zoar even unto Horonaim, as an heifer of three years old: for the waters also of Nimrim shall be desolate. 35- Moreover I will cause to cease in Moab, saith the LORD, him that offereth in the high places, and him that burneth incense to his gods. 36- Therefore mine heart shall sound for Moab like pipes, and mine heart shall sound like pipes for the men of Kir-heres: because the riches that he hath gotten are perished. 37- For every head shall be bald, and every beard clipped: upon all the hands shall be cuttings, and upon the loins sackcloth. 38- There shall be lamentation generally upon all the housetops of Moab, and in the streets thereof: for I have broken Moab like a vessel wherein is no pleasure, saith the LORD. 39- They shall howl, saying, How is it broken down! how hath Moab turned the back with shame! so shall Moab be a derision and a dismaying to all them about him.

48.28.0.en: Shouting (uproar): noise and clamor. Since the Babylonians seized the good things of Moab and its gardens full of fruitful trees, the Moabites were in great sorrow, for they no longer had vineyards, and the enemies also demolished the winepresses. Instead of hearing in Moab the shout of joy at gathering the harvests, pressing the vines and drawing out the wine, the noise of weeping will be heard, especially since the men who tread the grapes in the winepresses have died at the hand of Babylon.

48.29.0.en: Heshbon: the capital of Moab, lying in its north.

48.29.1.en: Elealeh: a Moabite city lying on a hill north of Heshbon.

48.29.2.en: Jahaz: a Moabite city lying east of the Dead Sea.

48.29.3.en: Zoar: beside Sodom and Gomorrah, and it was not burned with them because Lot took refuge in it; it lies south-east of the Dead Sea.

48.29.4.en: Horonaim: a Moabite city lying in a plain beside Zoar. The waters of Nimrim: many springs lying south-east of the Dead Sea.

48.29.5.en: Heifer of three years old: a heifer three years of age.

48.29.6.en: Weeping and sorrow filled the Moabites, as cries of distress rose from the various places of Moab, from the capital of Moab, Heshbon, and from all the land, however rich in its good things, for the enemy had plundered all these good things.

48.30.0.en: The Moabites lost their hope in their gods, since they did not help them in Babylon’s attack on them, so they abandoned the worship of idols in despair of them, but they did not return to God. Thus no incense was offered in the temples of the idols, and no worship on the high places to the pagan gods.

48.31.0.en: Jeremiah expresses his sorrow over the cities of Moab, such as Kir-heres, by sounding like a sad pipe for them because they have lost their riches.

48.32.0.en: The sorrow of Moab appears in the shaving of the men’s hair; those who shaved used to do this to captives. They also shave their beards, which symbolize dignity, that is, the Moabites become humbled and abased.

48.33.0.en: Weeping and sorrow filled the houses of the Moabites, where they went up and wept on their roofs; instead of offering pagan worship on the roofs, they offered weeping and humiliation, and the streets were filled with weepers. For God had broken Moab by means of Babylon, and He likens Moab to an old vessel unfit for use, which its owner breaks.

48.34.0.en: The pride of Moab turned into weakness and lowliness. They fled before Babylon and gave it their backs, and Moab became an example of mockery before those around it, and also of terror and fear, for how was the mighty one shattered, so that all the cities feared Babylon’s violence against them if it attacked them.

48.34.1.en: When troubles press on you, do not give way to despair, but take refuge in God, rejecting everything you relied on, and you will experience the power of God in your life, and He will rescue you from your troubles.

48.34.3.en: 40- For thus saith the LORD; Behold, he shall fly as an eagle, and shall spread his wings over Moab. 41- Kerioth is taken, and the strong holds are surprised, and the mighty men’s hearts in Moab at that day shall be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.

48.34.4.en: 42- And Moab shall be destroyed from being a people, because he hath magnified himself against the LORD. 43- Fear, and the pit, and the snare, shall be upon thee, O inhabitant of Moab, saith the LORD. 44- He that fleeth from the fear shall fall into the pit; and he that getteth up out of the pit shall be taken in the snare: for I will bring upon it, even upon Moab, the year of their visitation, saith the LORD. 45- They that fled stood under the shadow of Heshbon because of the force: but a fire shall come forth out of Heshbon, and a flame from the midst of Sihon, and shall devour the corner of Moab, and the crown of the head of the tumultuous ones. 46- Woe be unto thee, O Moab! the people of Chemosh perisheth: for thy sons are taken captives, and thy daughters captives. 47- Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days, saith the LORD. Thus far is the judgment of Moab.

48.35.0.en: He likens the army of Babylon, in its swift attack and its swooping on Moab, to the eagle that swoops swiftly from the sky on its prey.

48.36.0.en: A woman in her pangs: the woman at the hour of her childbirth. Kerioth: a fortified Moabite city lying south of the river Arnon. By Babylon’s attack they seized the fortified cities and all the land of Moab, and the strong Moabite soldiers were in great weakness, like the woman who writhes at the hour of her childbirth.

48.37.0.en: The reason for the destruction of Moab and the perishing of its people is its pride against God and His people, the children of Israel.

48.38.0.en: The Moabites are struck with great fear and die of fear, and whoever escapes death by fear falls, as he flees from Babylon, into pits found on the road and dies; and whoever is able to escape these pits falls into the snares that Babylon made for them to make them fall, and they perish also. This is because God commanded their punishment for the multitude of their evils at this time, that is, this year.

48.39.0.en: When the Moabites fled from the village of Moab, they took refuge in their capital Heshbon, and were surprised to find it burning at the hand of Babylon, so their escape was lost.

48.40.0.en: The sum is the perishing of the Moabite people who worship Chemosh, with their men and women, at the hand of Babylon.

48.41.0.en: What is meant by the bringing again of the captivity of Moab is not the establishment of a state for them, but the faith of the captive Moabites in Christ, so that they live a new life in the faith.

48.41.1.en: The devil, with his great power and the speed of his swooping on men, cannot do anything if he has no place in them. So beware, my brother, of sin, lest you fall into it, and if you fall, turn back from it by repentance, and the devil will fear you and keep away from you.

48.41.2.en: Prophecies about the children of Ammon, Edom, Damascus, the Arabs and Elam
